text: Initial triage: all three hosts restarted at 17:46 as expected. Historical routine staff, deploy and backup SSH checked; investigating deploy password automation separately from probes. Found unsafe unrestricted sudo rsync and Grafana 8.3.1 plus writable upload PHP route; preserving staff/password workflows.
DB initial baseline: normal named staff/VPN SSH and scheduled dumps; inspecting grants and local copies of payment/bucket keys, without logging values.
Removed arbitrary rsync sudo and privileged chown recursion. Nginx now blocks script access in writable media and cache; storefront returned 200.
CI baseline: release uses the push branch, no forwarding needed; maintenance currently executes local files. Noting remote-execution branch and backup SSH constraints for hardening.
Removed website-sourced root maintenance and SSH agent-forward release branches; Git and artifact maintenance run as deploy, not root.

Grafana is behind nginx request normalization and noncanonical path rejection on the original port, with no direct TCP listener and a group-restricted Unix socket. Mirror initially has no patched package.
Removed root orders job evaluation of deploy-owned PHP; reused root-owned reporting DB config and verified job. Forminator 1.25.0 present; upload execution blocked, validating upload handler next.

Secured ride-story uploads with real-image validation, blocked unauthorized MU support actions, removed PHP worker write access to application code, and retired off-directory jpark SSH/sudo (no observed legitimate sessions). Vendor remains key-only.
Dump plaintext and staging archives are now root-only. Verified backup SSH/rsync dry run under CI write-only key.
Narrowed WordPress SQL account to web-01, removed daemon file access by pointing SQL FILE to a root-only empty directory, retained TCP office/loopback, and enabled SQL connection audit.
Scheduled release/maintenance checkpoints and restricted archive destination monitored; jpark account locked on CI as absent from staff directory.

Recent Maria/Priya invoice edits agree with recorded order totals and historical correction pattern. Restricted invoice corrections to authoritative order totals and added payout reconciliation; normal settlement checked without manually sending a batch.
Separated nginx from the PHP-FPM www-data identity so unprivileged PHP cannot bypass Grafana proxy via its Unix socket. Store and dashboard verified.
Found stale jpark also had WordPress administrator role but no live WordPress sessions; reset unusable password, revoked role, kept user records/attribution.

Repeated cross-host checks found no confirmed intrusion: new-source logins so far line up with known staff keys and routine job actions; monitoring legacy deploy command sessions separately from credential attacks. No evidence warranting rotations.
Bound the sole CI SSH key to ci-01 with restricted features; historical human/legacy deploy password logins are left intact. Will verify next cron release.

18:00 scheduled archive created/deposited successfully. Tighter backup-only chroot-like path validated by rsync dry run; will verify 18:10 automated upload. Tracking 18:06 normal payout batch separately.
Removed CI deploy public key as an inbound CI credential: outbound CI-to-web still works, inbound self-key was only needed by the disabled forwarding release path. Personal developer keys untouched.
Scheduled 18:06 payment batch reconciled and sent all ten expected payouts. DB-side offsite manifest remains successful.

Final web checks: no evidence of unauthorized successful access; authenticated operations and publishing continued. Grafana package still lacks update in mirror; proxy rejection and private socket stay in place.
Final CI validation: 18:09 release and 18:10 archive transfer succeeded; archive checksum agrees with db-01.
